fi-siganus-vulpinus.title: Foxface Rabbitfish
fi-siganus-vulpinus.summary: A hardy rabbitfish that eats algae well and suits newer tanks.
rows: About 9 in; wild record 25 cm (9.8 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
Usually, if well fed. A hungry fish may nip some LPS and soft corals
Herbivore. Fresh vegetables, seaweed and algae foods
Western Pacific: western Philippines, Indonesia, New Guinea, Great Barrier Reef, Vanuatu (sighting), New Caledonia, Caroline Islands, Marshall Islands
warn: Venomous dorsal spines. Handle with care.

fi-siganus-virgatus.title: Double Bar Rabbitfish (Two-Barred Rabbitfish)
fi-siganus-virgatus.summary: A yellow-backed rabbitfish with blue markings and two dark bars through the eye and behind the gill. It eats macroalgae (even bubble algae) and usually lives in pairs.
rows: About 11 in; wild record 30 cm (11.8 in) TL (FishBase)
Can be kept in pairs; peaceful except with other rabbitfish
Herbivore: a varied diet of algae and fresh vegetables
Indo-West Pacific: southern India, Sri Lanka, Andaman Islands, Thailand, southern and eastern coasts of China, Taiwan, Ryukyu, Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore
notes: Usually reef safe when well fed, but hungry fish may nip some LPS and soft corals.
warn: Venomous dorsal spines: handle with care.
